holes_found.description: The base-rate claim "hitting some recurrence somewhere inside that band is statistically near-certain by base rate" is asserted but not shown. Under a Poisson process with mean recurrence interval R in [200, 400] yr and band width W = 347 yr, expected event count is λ = W/R ∈ [0.87, 1.74], giving P(≥1) = 1 − e^(−λ) ∈ [0.58, 0.82]. "Near-certain" is justifiable at the lower-recurrence end (~83%) but is on the strong side at the upper-recurrence end (~58% — closer to "more likely than not" than "near-certain"). The clause's anticipated_objections (EXP-526) defends the framing under "reasonable assumptions about timing uniformity" and notes 3-5 expected events in the Hare 2018 window of ~1100yr, which under uniform spacing puts P(≥1 in the AD 1033-1380 band) at ~0.67-0.84 — supporting "near-certain" only at the upper end. A defender could counter "show me the math" and the math doesn't fully back the strong adverb. Recommend: either soften "near-certain" to "more probable than not" / "high-prior", OR add a parenthetical with the actual Poisson estimate (e.g., "P≈0.6-0.85 depending on assumed recurrence rate"). Either keeps the verdict intact without overclaiming.
holes_found.recommendation: In data/wins.json WIN-023 detail_verdict_text, replace "statistically near-certain by base rate" with "more probable than not under any reasonable base-rate model" OR append a parenthetical like "(under Poisson statistics with mean recurrence 200-400yr and a 347yr band, P≥1 event ≈ 0.58-0.82)". Minor.

holes_found.description: Structural fuzziness in the "wide window" framing. The clause constructs the historicist target band as AD 1033-1380, then concludes "The dome's apparent ~50-year fit is selection of one recurrence inside a wide window, not a tight prediction." But ~950 AD is OUTSIDE the constructed AD 1033-1380 band (by ~83yr at the closest historicist anchor, AD 1033). A sharp defender could read this as either (a) curmudgeon contradicting itself — if the band excludes AD 950, then the dome event is REFUTED, not Unfalsifiable; or (b) curmudgeon implicitly expanding the band to include AD 950 without saying so. The argument is salvageable — the intended reading is that the dome's "5% miss to AD 1000" target is itself selection (AD 1000 corresponds to no actual theological anchor — it's just the calendar millennium derived from Dionysius Exiguus's 6th-century AD-numbering convention), and ANY band wide enough to encompass the AD 950 event would be wider still than 347yr, making the base-rate hit even more certain. But the clause doesn't make this chain explicit. Recommend: one connector sentence after the four anchors, e.g., "Note that AD 1000 — the figure the defender's '5% miss' implicitly assumes — corresponds to none of these historicist anchors; it is the calendar millennium fixed by Dionysius Exiguus's 6th-century AD-numbering, not a theological event." That closes the loop. Minor — argument as written is broadly correct but a careful reader will pause at the apparent inconsistency.
holes_found.recommendation: Insert one sentence after the four historicist anchors that explicitly notes AD 1000 is not on the historicist menu (it is a calendar artifact, not a theological event). Optional. The clause works as-is for most readers; the sentence would harden it against a sharp defender.

holes_found.description: The four historicist anchors are presented as "mainstream" without sourcing. A reader unfamiliar with Christian eschatology may not know that Constantine (AD 313), Nicaea (AD 325), and Theodosius (AD 380) have all been proposed as millennial starts within historicist/preterist Christian traditions. The dates themselves are well-known historical events and don't need inline citation, but the categorical claim "mainstream historicist anchor points" is curmudgeon-asserted. A defender could object: "This is your taxonomy, not standard. Show me a peer-reviewed source that lists these four as standard millennial anchors." The EXP-526 anticipated_objections does address this ("competing historicist starting points which they have been in mainstream Christian eschatology since at least the 4th century") but no citation is offered in the published text. Recommend: optionally cite a reference work (e.g., the Oxford Handbook of Millennialism, Walls 2008) for the historicist anchor diversity claim. Minor.
holes_found.recommendation: Optional: add a short citation reference in detail_verdict_text or in detail_extra for the historicist millennial-anchor diversity. Not blocking — the claim is defensible without it, but a single scholarly reference would close the rhetorical gap.

stronger_arguments.description: The strongest possible base-rate framing would explicitly note that AD 950 itself is OUTSIDE the legitimate historicist target band (AD 1033-1380). This actually weakens the dome's claim — the dome event is not even within the historicist range, only within the calendar-millennium range (AD 1000 ± 50). The dome's "5% miss" framing thus relies on a target (AD 1000) that has no theological basis — it's just calendar arithmetic from Dionysius Exiguus. Reframing the verdict text to spotlight this — "the dome's apparent ~50yr fit is to a target (AD 1000) that doesn't appear on any historicist menu; against actual historicist targets the event MISSES by 83yr (closest, AD 1033) to 430yr (farthest, AD 1380)" — would harden the verdict further. Current text correctly classifies this as unfalsifiable; the proposed sharpening would make the post-hoc retrodiction nature even more visible. (See hole #2 recommendation.)

The dome's failure to monitor this WIN (monitor.py has no domain for it; data/wins.json:WIN-023.code_analysis.monitoring='none') is structurally important: among the 72 WINs, the un-monitored ones are concentrated in the theological/categorical category (compare WIN-031 verdict='Unfalsifiable'). This pattern — monitoring=none correlates with categorical/theological claims — is a stronger argument than per-WIN debunking. Currently Part 2b cites monitoring stats. Suggest cross-referencing WIN-023 → Part 2b in stronger language: "The dome's automation does not even attempt to validate this WIN — it's a paragraph in 02-wins.txt with no comparison logic. The CONFIRMED stamp is self-awarded."

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome correctly identifies that ~950 AD is a real archaeomagnetic event (data/wins.json:WIN-023.detail_evidence cites Campuzano 2019 SHAWQ2k at doi:10.1016/j.epsl.2019.01.050 and Tarduno 2015 at doi:10.1038/ncomms8865). Both sources confirm late-first-millennium emergence of the current reversed-flux patch. The new EXP-526 clause correctly identifies that a millennial-anchor prediction is in principle falsifiable — if archaeomagnetic data had shown emergence ~AD 500 or ~AD 1500, the millennial-match would have failed (per EXP-526.kernel_of_truth). This concession to the dome's argument structure is honest scholarship — we do not strawman.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The match is not from dome physics — the date is adopted from published literature, not derived (data/wins.json:WIN-023.code_analysis.derives_from_dome=false; raw-text/06-evolution.txt:16 admits "Completely failed to mathematically reconcile SAA splitting"). The new EXP-526 clause sharpens the unfalsifiability by showing that the theological t=0 is itself non-unique (target band AD 1033-1380 under historicist anchors, effectively unbounded under amillennial reading) — so the apparent ~50yr fit is selection of one figure in a wide menu, not a tight prediction. The Hare 2018 archaeomagnetic recurrence pattern (doi:10.1002/2017GL076007, recurrences in 425-1550 CE per the Crossref-verified paper title) makes hitting some recurrence inside any reasonable band a high-prior outcome by base rate. Three minor holes flagged above tighten the wording but do not undermine the verdict.

deeper_analysis: EXP-526 is a structurally sound argument-hardening patch. It does what it set out to do: defends the Unfalsifiable verdict against the strongest defender objection ("~50yr miss out of 1000yr = 5%, impressive") by showing the target band is much wider than "AD 1000 ± 50yr". The four-historicist-anchor enumeration is solid (AD 33 resurrection, AD 313 Edict of Milan, AD 325 Council of Nicaea, AD 380 Edict of Thessalonica — all historical dates are correct; all are recognized as candidate millennium starts in historicist Christian eschatology). The Hare 2018 base-rate framing is qualitatively correct but quantitatively soft ("near-certain" overclaims at the upper-recurrence end of the 200-400yr interval — see hole #1). Structural fuzziness in the "wide window" framing (hole #2): the constructed band AD 1033-1380 excludes AD 950, so the clause is implicitly arguing either (a) AD 950 is OUTSIDE the legitimate historicist band (which would support REFUTED, not Unfalsifiable) or (b) ANY band loose enough to admit AD 950 must be wider than 347yr and the base-rate argument is even stronger. Intended reading is (b); explicit statement would harden against a sharp defender. None of these holes rise above minor — the verdict (Unfalsifiable) is well-supported and the new clause materially improves WIN-023's defensibility. Advocate-mode: the strongest remaining defender attack on the clause is "your anchor selection is curmudgeon-curated — show me a peer-reviewed taxonomy of historicist millennium anchors that matches your four" (hole #4). This is mitigated by EXP-526's anticipated_objection #1 ("competing historicist starting points which they have been in mainstream Christian eschatology since at least the 4th century") but a citation would close the loop. Total defense_survives_count: 2 (out of 5 strongest defender lines I could construct) — well below the 3+ threshold that would trigger a defense-neutralization EXP. Recommended action: no_change. The clause does its job; the four minor holes are polish-grade, not structural.

advocate_mode.best_defense: Your new t=0-anchor-non-uniqueness clause introduces three weaknesses you can be attacked on: (1) the four historicist anchors are your selection — a different curator might choose AD 0 (calendar zero → AD 1000), AD 70 (destruction of Jerusalem → AD 1070), or AD 538 (rise of Roman papacy in Reformer historicism → AD 1538), producing a different band. Your taxonomy is post-hoc curated to widen the target. (2) The base-rate calculation is hand-waved. You say "near-certain" but show no math — under Poisson statistics with the Hare 2018 ~200-400yr recurrence and a 347yr band, P(≥1) is 0.58-0.82, which is "more likely than not" but not "near-certain" at the upper end. (3) Your constructed band (AD 1033-1380) excludes AD 950 entirely — so by your own argument, the dome event is actually a MISS to the legitimate historicist band, not a fit inside it. This either supports REFUTED (your own band excludes the event) or it shows you're implicitly arguing the band must be wider to include AD 950 (in which case state that explicitly). The clause as written has an internal tension you haven't resolved. None of these break the Unfalsifiable verdict — the structural argument about t=0 looseness is solid — but they invite a careful reader to push back on the specific wording.
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Tighten the base-rate phrasing ("near-certain" → "more probable than not") and add a one-sentence note that AD 950 sits below the historicist band entirely, so the apparent 5% fit is to a calendar-zero target (AD 1000) that corresponds to no theological event. These are the two highest-leverage edits; the four-anchor taxonomy citation is optional polish.
